title: PackManifest

after.description: Mods it loads after when they run, by alias; they take no version.

breaks.description:
Mods it cannot run beside, by alias; with a `version`, only those
versions.

description.description: One sentence on what it adds.

enshwick.description:
The Enshwick releases it is made for, as a Cargo-style version
requirement such as `=1.0.0-alpha.12` (empty for any); a loader of
another release skips the pack and names both.

exports.description:
What other mods may use, each `event:<name>` for an event its scripts
define, `point:<name>` for a point of `[[point]]` or `content:<name>`
for its content: `event:greeted` lets them hear `<id>:greeted`. The
loader refuses them anything else of the pack's.

homepage.description: Where players read about it, an `https://` address.

id.description:
The pack id, `<author>.<name>` like a mod's; it names the folder, the
namespace of the pack's content and its settings folder in each world.

name.description: The name players read; the id when empty.

point.description: The extension points its scripts own and define at start.

requires.description:
Mods and packs it needs, by the aliases its files and scripts know
them by; the loader runs them first and leaves the pack off without
them.

setting.description:
The pack's settings, in the order the Mods screen shows them; a Luau
mod reads them, as a Rust mod reads its `Config`.

version.description: A Cargo-style version requirement; empty for any.

oneOf.description: Links see the answer and change nothing.
Links may change the answer; the owner may ignore the change.
Links may change the answer, and the owner takes it.

anyOf.description: The mod's id alone, for any version.
The mod's id with a version requirement.

doc.description: What the point decides, for other mods' definitions.

input.description: The input's fields, laid out in this order without padding.

mode.description: How links act on the answer.

name.description:
The local name, 1 to 128 of `[a-z0-9_./-]`: `price` is the point
`<pack id>:price`.

output.description: The answer's type, one of the field types.

refusable.description: Whether a link may refuse, which stops the chain.

PackPointField.description:
One field of a [`PackPoint`]'s input.

# Examples

See [`PackPoint`].

doc.description: What it holds, for other mods' definitions.

type.description:
Its type: a number such as `u32` or `f32`, `bool`, or one of the
API's ids such as `enshwick.item_id`.

PackSetting.description:
One setting of a pack, a `[[setting]]` table of `pack.toml`.

# Examples

```
use enshwick::packs::PackManifest;

let manifest = PackManifest::parse(r#"
id = "you.greeter"
version = "1.0.0"

[[setting]]
key = "greeting"
default = "Welcome"
doc = "What a player who joins reads."

[[setting]]
key = "every"
default = 30
min = 1
"#)?;
let schema = manifest.settings_schema().ok_or("no settings")?;
assert_eq!(schema.fields[1].min, Some(1.0));
# Ok::<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>>(())
```

choices.description: The values it accepts; empty for any.

default.description: The value on first start; its type is the setting's.

doc.description: What it does, for the file's comments and the Mods screen.

key.description: The key in the settings file, of `[a-z0-9_]`.

text.description:
The key of its translated label in the pack's `texts.toml`;
`config.<key>` unless said.

PackSide.description:
Where a pack runs, in `pack.toml`.

# Examples

See [`PackManifest`].

oneOf.description:
Where the world runs and on every client playing in it, which must
run the same pack, files and all: the default, as both read content.

Only where the world runs: the dedicated server, or a client that
hosts or plays alone, such as a pack of loot alone.
